newsitem.title: USA: Republic Engineered Steels says to cut jobs.
newsitem.headline: Republic Engineered Steels says to cut jobs.

text.p: Republic Engineered Steels Inc said Wednesday it plans to eliminate more than 500 jobs this calendar year and has restructured into three units.

The steelmaker earlier reported an adjusted net loss of $0.36 for the second quarter ended Dec 31, versus an adjusted $0.03 net loss in the year-ago period. Both figures exclude an after-tax effect of employee stock plan charges.

"In light of severe pricing pressures and Republic's financial performance, management is immediately undertaking the initial steps necessary to cut costs commensurate with falling prices," chairman Russell Maier said in a statement.
The stock was up 1/8 to 2-3/8 on Nasdaq.
Republic said it will reduce its salaried workforce by more than 200 and its plant force by more than 300.
Effective immediately, Republic said its hot rolled bar, cold finished bar and stainless/specialty steels divisions become stand-alone units accountable for their own results.

The quarter's results reflect a continuing decline in selling prices, Republic said. Shipments in the quarter rose to 232,400 tons from 204,000 tons but average selling prices fell 11.3 percent to $752 a ton from $848 a ton, it said.

The decline in average selling price far outstripped cost cuts and raw material cost declines, it said, adding that the mix of steel sold included more lower margin semi-finished carbon and alloy steel and less higher margin, value-added cold finished and specialty steels than the year-ago quarter.
Further, it said, it lowered prices on a high-quality bar product to defend market share against new competitors.

Republic has 10 plants in Ohio, Pennsylvania, Connecticut, Maryland, Indiana and Illinois, including a $165 million continuous casting complex opened in 1995. Republic was formed in 1989 when Maier led an employee purchase of LTV Corp's Steel Bar Division including the old Republic Steel.
